title: 17,000 Tickets and a ₹100-Crore Gamble: The Spy Universe Has Never Opened This Quietly
excerpt: Alpha releases tomorrow with the weakest advance booking in YRF Spy Universe history. Alia Bhatt's spy thriller needs a miracle — or extraordinary word-of-mouth — to avoid becoming the franchise's first single-digit opener.
body:
There is a version of tomorrow where Alpha opens to a thunderous reception and the YRF Spy Universe proves it can carry a female-led franchise. There is also a version where it becomes the quietest opening the spy universe has ever seen.

Right now, the numbers suggest we're headed for version two.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0

The Advance Booking Problem

With less than 24 hours to go before Alia Bhatt, Sharvari, Bobby Deol, and Anil Kapoor hit screens in the franchise's most ambitious swing yet, Alpha has registered advance bookings worth just ₹69.02 lakh — excluding blocked seats — across 3,347 shows nationwide. Over 17,600 tickets have been sold. Delhi leads the charge at ₹17 lakh, followed by Maharashtra at ₹16 lakh.

For context: Alia's last theatrical release, *Jigra*, clocked ₹1.70 crore in final day-one advance bookings. Alpha needs a 146% jump in the next few hours just to match that — and *Jigra* wasn't exactly a blockbuster. Industry insiders who were predicting a near-₹10 crore opening have quietly revised their numbers downward. The current forecast sits between ₹4.5 and ₹6 crore net, which would make Alpha the lowest-opening film in the entire spy universe. That's a franchise that includes *Pathaan* (₹57 crore day one), *War* (₹53 crore), and *Tiger 3* (₹44 crore). Single digits would be unprecedented for a YRF Spy Universe film.

> "The current forecast sits between ₹4.5 and ₹6 crore net, which would make Alpha the lowest-opening film in the entire spy universe."

What's Going Wrong — and What Might Go Right

The elephant in the auditorium is Welcome To The Jungle, which is six days into its run, holding 11,000 shows daily, and showing no signs of releasing its grip on screens. Akshay Kumar's franchise comedy has already crossed ₹128 crore worldwide. Exhibitors only have so many screens to give, and right now, *Welcome To The Jungle* is occupying them.

![Spy Universe — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/d/d6/YRF_Spy_Universe_logo.jpg)

There's also the question of novelty. The spy universe has conditioned audiences to expect a specific formula: a male superstar, slick action set-pieces, a massive opening weekend. Alpha upends that. Alia Bhatt plays Sita, an assassin dismantling her stepfather's illicit soldier programme, with Sharvari as a rival operative and Bobby Deol as the villain — the internet's beloved "Lord Bobby," now operating on full menace. Anil Kapoor rounds out the ensemble as the Chief of R&AW. The film runs 140 minutes and carries a ₹100-crore budget.

Director Shiv Rawail — making his feature debut with arguably the highest-pressure launchpad in Hindi cinema — has a trump card up his sleeve: a Hrithik Roshan cameo, reprising his role as Kabir Dhaliwal from *War*. Whether that's enough to drive walk-in audiences remains the question.

> YRF's strict instructions to exhibitors: ticket prices must match Welcome To The Jungle. First screenings start no earlier than 9:30 AM. This is a controlled, premium release — not a desperate bid for volume.

Why It Still Matters

Here's the thing about Alpha that the advance booking numbers can't capture: this is the first female-led action franchise film to come out of the spy universe. It's the seventh installment, and every previous entry has been built around a male lead — SRK, Hrithik, Salman, Tiger Shroff. Alia Bhatt stepping into that space isn't just a casting choice; it's a structural bet that the audience will follow a woman through the same mayhem, the same scale, the same universe.

If Alpha's word-of-mouth is strong — if the action delivers, if Bobby Deol's villainy lands, if that Hrithik cameo sends the theatre into hysteria — the opening-day number won't matter. *Cocktail 2* opened at ₹14.1 crore and has since crossed ₹151 crore worldwide on the back of sheer audience love. Walk-in audiences have rescued films before.

But if Alpha stumbles, it could do real damage to the idea that a female-led spy film can command the same real estate as a *Pathaan* or a *War*. And that would be a loss for more than just YRF's balance sheet. It could also impact the broader conversation around female representation in Indian cinema, a topic of increasing importance to diaspora audiences who often look to Bollywood for evolving cultural narratives.

For the Diaspora

Alpha releases globally on July 3 — screens are confirmed across North America, the UK, the Middle East, and Australia. For NRI audiences who've been tracking the spy universe since *Ek Tha Tiger*, this is the most consequential opening in the franchise's history. Not because of the budget. Not because of the stars. But because of what a strong opening — or a weak one — says about what kind of heroes the audience is willing to buy a ticket for. Many in the diaspora, particularly younger generations, are keen to see Indian cinema reflect more diverse and empowering roles for women, moving beyond traditional portrayals. The success or failure of *Alpha* will be closely watched as a barometer for this shift.

The counters open tomorrow morning. Everything Alpha becomes starts then.
author: Diaspora Desk
